thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High rate of container restarts in serving-runtime-gpu-pool (eu-west). Autoscaler recently spun up nodes; now multiple pods showing OOMKilled / CUDA errors. Impact: elevated 5xx on hosted endpoints, some customers reporting timeouts. Paging oncall.

alex: ack, I'm on it. Looking at node events + kubelet logs now. Can someone check recent autoscaler commit? I saw a config change earlier to aggressive scale-down.

kirti: oncall-sre here, joining. I see rapid scale up/down in the last 4m: node-add -> pods scheduled -> immediate OOMKilled / crashloop on runtime containers. Possible bad image or kernel-driver mismatch.

dana: eng-runtime, noted a night deploy of a new memory optimizer image at 22:12 UTC that toggled batch_prefetch to true. That could increase memory for some models. Rolling that back in progress if we confirm correlation.

lauren: CS/Support reporting customers A and B saw errors on text-generation endpoints ~22:15 UTC. Raising severity to Sev2 until we have mitigation.

ml-bot: quick telemetry summary: 73% of restarts show container exit code 137; 22% show CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED. Mean memory used on affected pods ~11.8 GiB, node gpu memory capacity 12 GiB.

alex: paste of recent pod logs:
```
E tensorflow: cudnn failed to allocate workspace
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
[2026-03-15T22:16:02Z] Runtime: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED
```

kirti: that points to GPU driver/userland mismatch or a small memory leak + aggressive packing. Also autoscaler is packing many low-concurrency pods on same node. Need to stop scale-down and pin current capacity.

ops-bot: Runbook step triggered: "Serving GPU OOM / crashloop". Suggested immediate actions: 1) Disable autoscaler scale-down, 2) set node pool min to current, 3) add taint to isolate new nodes, 4) rollback runtime image if confirmed.

alex: executing: `kubectl annotate --overwrite ns/serving autoscaler.redwood/scale-allowed=false` then `gcloud container clusters update --min-nodes=8 --region=eu-west` (commands logged). Will also cordon one highly churned node for investigation.

dana: rollback started: set image tag back to v3.2.1 -> v3.2.0 for serving-runtime. Creating canary with reduced batch size env: `MODEL_BATCH_SIZE=1` to test memory profile.

lauren: notifying impacted customers, set expectation: degraded throughput, retrying will see errors. CS has posted status page update draft with incident id INC-20260315-01.

kirti: note: autoscaler metrics show ephemeral spikes in pod creation rate due to traffic bursts + aggressive minReplicas=0 policy. Suggest change: set minReplicas=2 for critical pools and bump stabilizationWindow to 5m.

alex: draining node gpu-7-az1 to repro locally, capturing dmesg:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: Failed to allocate channel
[ 1234.567893] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
```

ml-bot: performance note: a recent quantization change in v3.2.1 increased transient workspace for certain kernels; on older driver versions that can push memory over limit causing cudnn alloc failures.

dana: confirmed: v3.2.1 uses cuDNN workspace growth heuristic. If node drivers are 11.4 and binary built with 11.6 bits, we see allocation mismatches. Ops, can we revert the kernel module on affected nodes to 11.6 or pin the runtime to use smaller workspace?

ops-bot: we can roll node drivers but that's high-risk during incident. Prefer to rollback runtime image to v3.2.0 which is already happening. Also starting targeted redeploy to avoid packing many pods on same GPU: set podAntiAffinity and lower `max-packed-models` to 1 temporarily.

alex: mitigation checklist executed: autoc.scale-down disabled, cluster min nodes raised, runtime rollback started, podAntiAffinity patch applied to # critical deployments. Monitoring for new restarts.

kirti: can we add a temporary admission webhook to reject pods with MODEL_BATCH_SIZE > 1 in this pool until stable? That would be surgical.

dana: good idea. I'll push a simple mutating webhook to inject env var MODEL_BATCH_SIZE=1 for namespace serving. Will follow up with PR for permanent guardrails.

lauren: update: customers A and C have been manually routed to regional fallback (us-east) with a degraded SLA. CS still triaging customers in eu-west only.

support-bot: posted incident ticker to #status-page and created INC-2026-0315-01. Notifying enterprise contacts for Dedicated customers in impacted region.

ml-bot: observability: error rate for generation endpoints dropped from 18% -> 7% in last 7 minutes after rollback kickoff and anti-affinity. Token latency still elevated for some flows.

alex: handing off to night oncall: @oncall-night please take this forward. I've documented steps taken in the incident doc and left commands in #inc-ops-log. I'll be available for 30m for context and escalation.

oncall-night: acknowledged. I'll keep autoscaler disabled, watch pod churn, and coordinate with ops for safe driver upgrade plan during maintenance window. Starting ∼30m watch.

kirti: assign postmortem: we need root cause on autoscaler policy + runtime change + driver mismatch. Action items: (1) Harden canary gating for runtime kernel changes, (2) enforce minReplicas for GPU pools, (3) add graceful backoff in autoscaler to avoid pack/unpack oscillation, (4) telemetry alert for CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED rate. I'll own (4).

dana: adding task to fix quantization heuristics and add runtime flag to cap cuDNN workspace.

lauren: CS follow-up: send customer post-incident summary within 24h, include mitigation, ETA for stable region. Also offer credits if SLA breached.

alex: closing note before handoff: severity remains Sev2, no data exfiltration, single region impact, mitigation stabilizing. Created postmortem stub: `/incidents/3605009876/pm-draft`. Night team will update.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-01 updated: status -> stabilizing, severity -> Sev2, assigned -> oncall-night. Logs and timeline collected automatically.

oncall-night: (final) I'm on watch. If we see restart rate > 5% over 5m or new CUDA errors spike, I'll page SRE escalation. Otherwise, continue with planned maintenance tomorrow to align drivers across nodes. :white_check_mark:
